title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling and connection draining
description: Introduces process signal listeners (SIGINT, SIGTERM) that close the HTTP server, stop accepting new requests, and wait for in‑flight requests to finish before exiting. This prevents abrupt termination, reduces dropped requests, and improves reliability in containerized deployments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while handling a long‑running request and verify the server stops accepting new connections but completes the in‑flight request before process exit
Send SIGINT when no active requests exist and ensure the server closes immediately and process exits with code 0
acceptance: The server must listen for SIGINT and SIGTERM, stop accepting new connections, wait up to 30 seconds for active requests to finish, then close and exit with code 0. If requests exceed the timeout, they are force‑closed and the process still exits. All existing unit and integration tests must continue to pass.
reason: Production environments (Docker, Kubernetes, serverless) rely on graceful shutdown to avoid data loss and improve uptime. Adding this feature aligns with the framework’s stability focus and eliminates a common operational pain point for users.
